# OS4 glass integration — current source boundary

Guiyuan's optional HyperOS 4 visual style incorporates an adapted subset of upstream MIUIX glass components. This folder documents **provenance and maintenance boundaries**, not an alternative build pipeline or a standalone library.

## Provenance and current dependency graph

- Published MIUIX baseline: `0.9.4-8972f941-SNAPSHOT` at `8972f941c194bd3c4e14c34543d5ebc7b39e40da`. The fallback vectors compile under `gy.os4.dialogSurfaces=false` against the same-revision source graph ([#1179 CI #41586552572](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/41586552572)). An independent clean build against these *published Maven binaries* was attempted without exposing GitHub credentials and stopped during dependency metadata resolution (`Username must not be null`, [#41587400064](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/41587400064)); this does **not** establish their availability or Kotlin ABI compatibility. A trusted authenticated check is still required if published fallback becomes a release gate.
- **Historical B1737 source-pinned graph (superseded by B1786):** [MIUIX Glass PR #423](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/pull/423) at `f4cfe9b0adaa5151b68ec169ed18d470b957a6f6` (previous accepted graph `b9f70838509fbc3f63f1a972777a7e6ce07f578f`). Guiyuan B1737 (`8f2f4bddc091f057b1f5dbbe07678f3cc7f9e20c`) passed [exact-head Full CI](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/41604585823), [isolated signed Canary verification](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/41605488416), and focused maintainer device acceptance. It was integrated into `dev` through [#1179](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1179) at `7eb025ddd99f00367377f8eaeadd6b155015c9e3`. **PR #423 was unmerged at B1737 acceptance and was merged to MIUIX `main` on 2026-11-07.** Device acceptance covers the tested app-local implementation, not direct replacement with the merged upstream Glass module or universal device compatibility.
- The CI composite build checks out the exact pinned core/UI/Blur/Preference/Nav source through [the repository action](../../.github/actions/miuix-source/action.yml); the same checkout contains Glass and Glass Icons. **The accepted app still uses app-local Glass UI bridges**; this is not end-to-end native `miuix-glass` adoption. Matched-source builds use native Glass action icons from the same-revision `miuix-glass-icons` module; `os4Published` retains pinned fallback vectors. B1737 is historical signed Canary evidence; B1786 is the later accepted app UI checkpoint described below. Neither verifies adoption of the directly linked `miuix-glass` module or a new Release. The native module transition must separately check ABI, interactions, ownership and shader fallback.
- Local Glass UI bridging source remains in `app/src/main/kotlin/top/yukonga/miuix/kmp/glass/`. OS4 action icons use `app/src/os4Upstream/kotlin/com/chaners/guiyuan/ui/icons/Os4NativeGlassIcons.kt` for native same-revision vectors and preserve pinned vector fallback under `app/src/os4Published/kotlin/com/chaners/guiyuan/ui/icons/`. This is not a complete redistributed upstream Glass UI library.
- **Historical OS4 Share exception:** with accepted `b7a5f08f`, Diagnostics used ordinary `MiuixIcons.Share` in both UI styles because the old 24dp `Glass.Regular.Share` vector overfilled its viewport and was observed clipped in B1736. Candidate [#1370](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1370) uses the corrected upstream 28dp Glass Share in **OS4 style only**; OS3 style retains the ordinary icon. The 44dp button target and Share semantics are unchanged. Source compilation is verified, but device appearance is not yet accepted.
- Licensing and individual upstream attribution are recorded in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and preserved source headers. Do not remove SPDX/copyright notices from adapted files.

## Upstream merge checkpoint (2026-11-08)

- MIUIX [PR #423](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/pull/423) merged into `main` at `b7a5f08f5a8c20350406e1665a97fbf99b5d9c8c`. The exact-SHA upstream **Build All Tests** and **Publish to GitHub Packages** workflows succeeded; the latest tagged stable release remains `v0.9.4` (2026-09-20). Workflow success is not a verified Maven resolution or app-level acceptance.
- Relative to Guiyuan's **previous** source pin `f4cfe9b0`, later upstream Glass commits affect progressive top-bar backdrops, button materials and blur composition. Those Glass implementations have **not** replaced Guiyuan's app-local components; advancing the source checkout alone does not migrate them.
- **B1786 focused qualification:** [PR #1299](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1299) advances the same-source OS4 **UI/Nav/Blur/core dependency checkout** to `b7a5f08f5a8c20350406e1665a97fbf99b5d9c8c`. Comparing repository trees against `f4cfe9b0` found only `Component.kt` (unbounded-width sizing), `NavSwipeDismiss.kt` (consumed-release cancellation) and one navigation test changed in the included runtime modules; the build catalog's AGP 9.5.1 is guarded and normalized to Guiyuan's 9.5.0. **No wholesale Glass module migration.** The app-local menu integrates upstream `GlassIconDropdownMenu` with isolated root-host exit coordination and five JUnit tests. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42427142011) and [signed Canary B1786](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42427816564) succeeded; the maintainer reported no problems after the requested device test, including the earlier B1783 low-saturation swipe regression. This is scoped device evidence, not general device certification. Two Codacy medium complexity alerts trace to the upstream-origin menu body and remain explicitly documented in the PR rather than blindly rewritten or suppressed.
- **Menu-source provenance (PR #1316):** the local OS4 Glass menu/transform chain was reconciled with upstream PR #423's accepted `b7a5f08f` source and its later `799d3d09` material-opacity correction. `GlassTransformPopup.kt` matches the latter revision byte-for-byte; the app-local `GlassIconButton.kt` keeps Guiyuan's already-used caller API and is not a verbatim upstream module replacement. The accepted source checkout for UI/Nav/Blur/core remains `b7a5f08f`, not a six-module `799d3d09` binary upgrade. Historical signed B1802 testing covered the menu migration scenarios reported as normal except an independent nested battery-color Sheet flash; signed B1805 was reported normal after its separate content-disposal ownership fix, which was integrated into `dev` through #1336. Consult PR #1316 for the menu branch's actual merge status and remaining acceptance scope.
- The isolated native-module compile probe [#1183](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1183) failed on public-API and Kotlin `internal` visibility boundaries. The merged Glass source still does not expose the app's compact/unclipped top-bar, preview/touch navigation, and cascade Back/host interaction contracts. Keep the accepted app-local bridge and its source pin until a bounded, source-matched module trial can meet these contracts without hidden upstream patches.

## Candidate: 28dp Glass iconography at `ea1b935d` (not adopted)

MIUIX [`ea1b935d`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/commit/ea1b935ddba7bb25de816342b2e7a4ad2113bb46) establishes a **28dp Glass vector canvas** and matching viewport/group coordinates while ordinary MIUIX icons remain 24dp and standard Glass top-bar buttons remain 44dp. Its `GlassPopupItem` takes `maxOf(24.dp, icon.defaultWidth/Height)` on each axis instead of forcing an icon into 24dp. The official [`Build All Tests`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42486425937) and [`Example App`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42486425918) workflows passed on that SHA; that does **not** verify a complete published dependency graph.

Guiyuan [Draft PR #1370](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1370) carries the official 28dp Back, Search, Close, Filter, More, Refresh, Edit, Copy, Delete and Share vectors across the native and fallback source sets, plus corresponding OS4 call-site sizes and the exact upstream popup implementation. Six existing fallback PathNode sequences match upstream; four newly ported builders (Edit/Copy/Delete/Share) match byte-for-byte. OS3 style retains ordinary icons and 24dp presentation; the local Glass navigation icon was already 28dp and its preview/touch extension remains local.

**Verification:** exact-source [CI #42488503263](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42488503263) built the native source path. [CI #42490415128](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/actions/runs/42490415128) additionally compiled `gy.os4.dialogSurfaces=false` with the same MIUIX source checkout; Debug assembly, unit tests and Codacy also passed. This **does not** establish independent resolution of the original published snapshot or newly published same-SHA POM/AAR metadata. [Upstream package publication](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42486425920) was still running at the last review. Device checks for Share, other Glass actions, popup/sheets, search, RTL, typography and light/dark remain unverified. PR #478 is not merged and its navigation animation is excluded. Do not promote the Draft candidate to `dev` on build evidence alone.

## Candidate: unified OS4 Glass at `ba0fca0` (not adopted)

**Decision: qualify later, do not upgrade.** The candidate is upstream commit [`ba0fca0cae3ace964eef59a3108cd782f7f9ec3d`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/commit/ba0fca0cae3ace964eef59a3108cd782f7f9ec3d). It is a **candidate source revision for one coherent, same-revision OS4 Glass dependency graph**, not an accepted artifact/version or authorization to replace local Glass code. Guiyuan's `miuix.upstream.revision`, published `miuix.version`/`miuix.revision`, CI checkout, runtime, and Build identity remain unchanged.

[Compared with the accepted `b7a5f08f` source](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/compare/b7a5f08f5a8c20350406e1665a97fbf99b5d9c8c...ba0fca0cae3ace964eef59a3108cd782f7f9ec3d), this revision adds two Glass-only commits across nine source/test files:
- [`799d3d09`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/commit/799d3d09f996d66cb2b1c2318deed8242c4f440e): separates button material-layer alpha from popup anchor visibility, with related Glass button/top-bar/popup changes and tests. A bounded correction from this commit is already represented in Guiyuan's **still-unmerged** menu migration [#1316](https://github.com/CHS-Haple/Guiyuan/pull/1316); this is not adoption of the whole Glass module.
- [`ba0fca0`](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/commit/ba0fca0cae3ace964eef59a3108cd782f7f9ec3d): retargets Glass navigation indicator drag/release to current geometry and adds dynamic-theme accent treatment, including new desktop interaction/colour tests. It does not itself establish Guiyuan's preview, touch-extension, compact top-bar or popup-host contracts.

**Evidence at the candidate checkpoint (2026-11-08):** the upstream exact-SHA [Build All Tests](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42464288102) is overall **failed**, although its Android `assembleAndroidTest` job passed; the JS/Wasm browser test job failed. The upstream [Example App build](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42464288107) is **failed**, including its Android job. The [Publish to GitHub Packages](https://github.com/compose-miuix-ui/miuix/actions/runs/42464288129) job was still in progress when checked. None of these results establishes that all required Android modules are officially published at the identical source revision, independently resolvable by Guiyuan, or app-compatible. Latest verified tagged stable release remained `v0.9.4`, not this SHA.

**Admission gates before a runtime dependency or module upgrade:**
1. Obtain trustworthy official **same-revision** Android POM/Gradle metadata and AAR artifacts for the complete resolved dependency graph (including the relevant UI, Blur, Core, Preference, Icons, Nav, Shader, Squircle, Glass and Glass Icons modules); prove actual Maven/GitHub Packages resolution, source-version provenance and compatible transitive versions. A successful publish workflow alone, cached sources, a locally synthesized SNAPSHOT, and mixed-revision modules are insufficient. Keep credentials inside the trusted resolution path.
2. Require successful/understood upstream **Android library and Android example** build evidence at the selected exact SHA. Investigate any other failed upstream matrix jobs rather than reporting an unqualified all-green result; assess API, AGP/Kotlin and source-to-binary compatibility independently.
3. On an isolated `feat/` or `refactor/` branch, attempt an atomic Glass module replacement only if the public API and Kotlin `internal` visibility boundaries can replace app-local same-package classes **without duplicate symbols or CI source rewriting**. Re-run a complete `base→HEAD` review and source-matched Guiyuan Android unit tests/Debug assembly/metadata checks. Do not point the protected CI checkout at an unqualified candidate.
4. Compare both UI styles' affected paths. For OS4: native/simplified button material alpha; top-bar clipping; popup/dismiss/Back, rapid reopen and cascades; drag interruptions, RTL and variable action count; theme/dynamic colours; bottom touch-safe zones and noninteractive preview; Sheet/Dialog lifecycle and backdrop; diagnostics Share exception. For OS3 **UI style**, verify common dependency contracts and absence of regression. No HyperOS 3 runtime support is implied.
5. Only after the above gates pass, use an explicitly reviewed same-SHA signed Canary checkpoint for focused Xiaomi 15 Pro interaction acceptance where runtime visuals changed. Do not allocate a Build or sign for this candidate tracking record. Promotion remains a separate review and `dev→main` decision.

Retain the current accepted source/published pins and local bridges until the complete gate passes. Monitor meaningful upstream fixes or an officially available matching artifact set without re-notifying unchanged/pending status.

## Maintenance contract

1. Check whether the upstream component is released, experimental or absent before changing a MIUIX-facing control.
2. Review its layout, state, gesture, scroll, inset, lifecycle and animation behavior against the **exact revision** selected for the build. Do not mix unrelated UI, Blur, Nav and glass implementations.
3. Compare OS3 and OS4 *UI styles* separately. The OS3 visual selector does **not** expand the advertised system support below HyperOS 4.
4. When the upstream module becomes suitable for adoption, compare ABI, transitive dependencies, screenshot/gesture parity, runtime fallback, performance and licensing before replacing local bridge code. Never auto-upgrade on upstream activity.
5. Keep experimental tests and source-matched signing separated from trusted publishing. Do not revive superseded OS4-only workflows.

## Native Glass module migration — source-based acceptance boundary (2026-11-03)

At the **2026-11-03 comparison checkpoint**, the accepted `dev` app contained **30 local Glass Kotlin files** (approximately 331 KiB) under `app/src/main/kotlin/top/yukonga/miuix/kmp/glass/`. A file-by-file comparison against **exact upstream PR #423 HEAD** `f4cfe9b0`, excluding comments and whitespace-only differences, found **24 files with the same implementation logic** (approximately 215 KiB). This is a duplication inventory, **not** proof that 24 files may individually be deleted: upstream and local classes share package-qualified names, and module-internal declarations have different visibility when compiled separately.

At that checkpoint, six implementation differences and their respective ownership decisions were:

| Local file | Relevant difference | Replacement decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GlassDropdownPopup.kt` | Local `handleBack` switch prevents the primary popup from competing with a visible submenu for Back; panel arguments otherwise align with upstream behavior. | Keep until the upstream cascade handles the same root-host/Back contract or an explicit public API provides this choice. |
| `GlassNavigationBar.kt` | Local `interactive` and `touchExtension` preserve noninteractive previews and extended bottom-area hit testing; Android inset behavior otherwise aligns. | Investigate caller-owned touch modifier and explicit enabled/semantics API; do not drop safe touch targets. |
| `GlassPopup.kt` | Selection checkmark tint and panel argument ordering differ. | Verify upstream selected/unselected visuals and popup composition semantics before replacing. |
| `GlassSecondaryPopup.kt` | Popup-surface modifier/interaction argument ordering differs, without a separately identified new owner. | Candidate for native reuse once the whole module is substituted. |
| `GlassTopAppBar.kt` | Local compact title/padding, `UiNativeTitleBar`, and unclipped navigation/action controls protect the verified OS4 top-bar layout. | Keep a small app-owned presentation adapter or ask upstream for the missing public extension points; do not remove clipping protections. |
| `GlassTransformPopup.kt` | Popup-surface modifier/interaction construction differed at this historical checkpoint. | Any future replacement must also honor the newer B1786 anchored-popup dismissal/host lifecycle contracts. |

**Current inventory boundary:** at the B1786/#1299 integration, `dev` has **31 local Glass Kotlin files**, including the new `GlassIconDropdownMenu.kt`; `GlassTransformPopup.kt` and the menu host lifecycle also changed. The six-item comparison above is **not a current full-file diff**. Regenerate source/ABI/diff evidence against the exact accepted revision before considering any deletion or module replacement.

**Dependency boundary:** the exact upstream checkout contains `miuix-glass`, and its KMP module depends on `miuix-ui`/`miuix-blur` plus navigation events. Guiyuan's current composite substitution includes UI, Blur, Nav, Icons, and Glass Icons, **not** `miuix-glass-android`. Adding that substitution alone would leave local duplicate class names; deleting selected files alone would break same-module internal references or app-specific API uses. An upstream merge or successful publish workflow does not, by itself, establish stable-release artifact availability or Guiyuan dependency compatibility.

**Deferred whole-module option (not part of the current plan):** only if separately requested and justified, trial the complete upstream Glass module on an isolated `refactor/*` branch, with all duplicate app-local Glass declarations excluded **atomically**. Place only genuinely app-specific behavior in a separate `com.chaners.guiyuan.ui` adapter/API layer, using stable public upstream APIs; where those APIs are absent, evaluate an upstream extension or defer adoption. Do **not** silently edit checked-out MIUIX Kotlin sources inside CI, copy six files into the upstream build, relax source-revision locks, or use an unverified binary fallback. Keep OS3-style behavior separate.

**Required evidence before merging a replacement:** (1) exact-revision Android compile and unit tests without duplicate classes or inaccessible `internal` API usage; (2) public API, source ownership, licensing, native/published fallback and transitive dependency review; (3) compare B1737 normal/cancelled Back, popup dismissal, rapid reopen, selected state, title clipping, bottom touch-safe zones and noninteractive preview; (4) light/dark and OS3/OS4 style switching; (5) one grouped signed Canary and maintainer device acceptance only if runtime UI behavior changes. A code-only/docs-only investigation does not consume a new Build.

**Alternatives rejected for this baseline:** continue manually copying all 30 files (high recurring drift), link native Glass alongside same-named local classes (duplicate symbols), or rewrite upstream checkout on CI (hidden third-party fork). Partial individual deletion is not a safe substitute for an owned module boundary.
